why: How long a test or developer path that spawns an Omnesis Gateway or an external harness host waits for its declared readiness condition. Most callers wait for /health; harness conformance waits for the loaded plugin service. One number, because independently chosen ones produced false reds: a suite that dies in its hook reports as a failed file with no failing test, which reads like a broken feature rather than a harness that stopped waiting. Sized for the slowest honest boot rather than the typical one — a cold tsx transform of the whole gateway on a machine running a full test lane. Nothing is served by failing fast here: a runtime that is never going to boot fails the surrounding hook either way, and every second shaved off this number buys nothing except a red tree on a loaded machine. Consumers must read this file rather than restate the number; scripts/gateway-boot-budget.test.mjs reddens if one drifts, and it reddens on a NEW runtime-readiness wait that does not read it — a fifth budget hiding in a second E2E harness is exactly how the first four happened.
